newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Facelift of Yeltsin's office cost Kremlin $292 mln.
newsitem.headline: Facelift of Yeltsin's office cost Kremlin $292 mln.

text.p: Russia spent $292 million to rebuild the Kremlin building housing President Boris Yeltsin's office and his administration, Interfax news agency said on Monday.
The agency quoted the Finance Ministry as saying in a letter to the lower house of parliament foreign contracters had earned $179 million from the complete makeover of the 18th century building.

The government paid Russian contracters 645 billion roubles ($112 million) in the 1993-96 project, the report said. This included restoring historic artistic details and adding the latest modern equipment to the structure housing the presidential administration.

The Russian government was able to continue to work on the building during a time it has struggled to fund vital programs, and has often lagged months behind in paying public sector workers from teachers to tax inspectors.
The building, next to the brick Kremlin wall facing Red Square, was once home to Bolshevik revolutionary Vladimir Lenin, but Yeltsin now lives outside the Kremlin and only keeps an office there.
